narrative.overview: This portfolio stages a career pivot as an audited, reconciled ledger rather than a generic developer-portfolio terminal. The subject is a Workday HR-transactions analyst (Cum Laude CS grad) moving into QA, Data Analysis, and AI — a pivot that is fundamentally about reconciliation and verification, so the interface borrows the visual grammar of that world: record IDs, verified/reconciled status marks, ruled ledger paper, and tabular data — rather than the halftone-dot, pixel-terminal aesthetic of a generic "indie dev" template it replaced. The system stays flat, quiet, and confident: one warm paper ground, near-black ink for text, and a single verification-green accent used sparingly and only where it means something (a completed record, an open-to-work status). Density is low and reading-first — this is a single scrolling document a recruiter skims in under a minute, not a dashboard. Two confirmed rejections carry forward from the redesign: no halftone/dot decoration, and no ruled-line background texture (tried once, explicitly rejected — the paper color and verified accent stay, decorative texture does not).
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, ledger-paper warmth, one verification-green accent used as real signal, not decoration
Every recurring numbered/entry label reads as a record ID (REC-01), not a decorative index
Pixel-font display headers (Geist Pixel) paired with a clean sans body and a monospace data voice
One primary action per view; no competing CTAs

rules.name: The Reserved Signal Rule
rules.body: Verified Green appears only on confirmed, evidence-backed states (a completed record, an "open to work" status). It never decorates a hover state, an icon, or a heading for emphasis alone — if it appears, something specific is being verified.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for genuinely tabular or identifier content — record IDs, dates, WPM stats, keyboard shortcuts. It is never used as a "technical-looking" costume on prose.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Shadows are reserved for content that must visually separate from the whole page (the command palette). A card, input, or badge never gets a shadow — a border and a background step do the job.

dos: Do reserve Verified Green for genuine verification/status signal (badges, checkmarks on evidence sections)
Do use monospace exclusively for record IDs, dates, and tabular data
Do keep exactly one primary (filled, pill) button per view; every other action is a plain text link
Do use 1px hairline borders and background-color steps for surface separation instead of shadows
donts: Don't reintroduce halftone/dot decoration or the ruled-line background texture — both were tried and explicitly rejected
Don't add shadows to cards, inputs, or badges; the command palette is the only surface allowed one
Don't let a section's record-ID number ("01", "02"...) carry meaning outside the homepage's own section sequence
Don't stack more than one filled/primary-weight CTA in the same view
